player_page.score_breakdown_unavailable: This score combines the player's shot volume, accuracy, finishing efficiency, sample size, and the strength of the opposing defence. The numeric breakdown of each component will be available at the next data update.
player_page.tooltip_shots_on_target: The heaviest-weighted component. Measured relative to the best player of the two teams in this match.
player_page.tooltip_shots_volume: The number of attempts, on target or not, relative to the highest volume of the two teams.
player_page.tooltip_finishing_efficiency: Their conversion rate compared to the average of the players in this match, smoothed when the sample is small.

player_page.tooltip_sample_reliability: Reduces the score when the player has few matches or few minutes. Equals 1 from five full appearances onward.
player_page.tooltip_opponent_context: Measures how permeable the opposing defence is. 1.00 = average defence; above that, a more favourable context for the goalscorer.

player_page.opponent_impact_intro: The threat score is not a fixed season profile : it is adjusted for the defence he's facing. Against {team}, the adjustment is {percent}.
player_page.opponent_impact_footer: The factor equals 1.00 against an average league defence. Above that, the defence concedes more than average ; below it, the defence is more solid. It is capped between 0.70 and 1.30.

about_page.hero_text: IASHARK analyses every match using real sports data from the current and previous seasons and a statistical score model. No martingale, no miracle system — the same method, applied in exactly the same way, match after match.
about_page.method_text: For each match, the system starts from both teams' real statistics over the current and previous seasons: goals scored and conceded, plus recent xG and shots when available. From these it estimates each team's expected goals, then the probability of every score with a Dixon-Coles model. For the 1X2, over/under 2.5 goals and both-teams-to-score markets, these probabilities are corrected by a calibration learnt from past seasons. Odds never enter this calculation.
about_page.card_history_text: The calculation uses the current season and the previous one. Early in the season, the previous season and a reference average carry more weight, then less and less as matches are played.
about_page.card_crossed_text: Probabilities come from a single score model (Dixon-Coles), calibrated on three markets. It is not a vote between models: the Poisson calculation and the simulation are only used to measure the agreement shown in the reliability indicator.
about_page.card_simulations_text: Each match is simulated 5,000 times (Monte Carlo method) to show the most likely scores. These simulations are not used to choose the bet.
about_page.card_reliability_text: A separate indicator combines agreement between the calculations, the quality of the available data and the number of matches played, for that specific match — it never changes the probability.
about_page.single_title: One model per match, no combo bets

No gut feeling.
Just data, a statistical model,

about_page.method_selection: The highlighted market is chosen automatically by a fixed rule: among the markets the model calculates and a bookmaker actually prices, the one with the highest estimated probability, preferably among those reaching a minimum price, and below a probability cap. A match that has already started, or is about to start when the calculation runs, gets no bet. The probability shown is the model's own, never adjusted afterwards. A language model then writes the explanatory text, but it does not calculate, choose or change any figure.
about_page.method_value: The gap with the market: the model then compares its probability with the one implied by the odds, once the bookmaker's margin is removed (Shin's method where possible). This gap is shown for information: it is not used to choose the market and guarantees no winnings.
about_page.single_text: At its core, the system analyses each match independently — one single bet at a time, never combinations of several bets.

demo_data.conseil_public: Under 1.5 first-half goals is the market best supported by this match's data: a 64% model probability, and first-half goal windows among the lowest of the match.
demo_data.analyse_card: The goals-by-window data confirm that the first half accounts for only 40% of total expected goals (14%+13%+13%), against 61% in the second half (19%+20%+22%). The Monte Carlo model has 1-1 as the most likely score at 10%, and 1-0 at 8%, which implies that a large majority of simulations stay at 0 or 1 goal at half-time. PSG show an xG of 1.94 over the whole match, which leaves little volume for the first half alone, especially as Monaco (#1) kept a clean sheet in their only away game this season.
demo_data.contexte: PSG are ranked #12 at home, with 2 consecutive draws in their recent form, while Monaco are ranked #1 away, with 2 consecutive wins and 1 clean sheet in 1 away match. PSG's xG stands at 1.94 for and 1.07 against, Monaco's at 1.60 for and 1.39 against, reflecting two attacking sides whose goal output is mostly concentrated in the second half.
demo_data.scenario_phase1: At kick-off, PSG (#12) settle in against Monaco (#1), two sides in contrasting form: the Parisians on 2 consecutive draws, the Monegasques on 2 wins in a row. The tactical intensity of the opening minutes creates little immediate danger, with the 0-15 min window showing a goal probability of just 14%.
demo_data.scenario_phase2: At half-time, the score remains tight and below the 1.5-goal threshold, confirming the statistical trend: Monaco have kept a clean sheet away from home (1 CS in 1 match), and PSG struggle to score early, with only 14% of their goals coming in the first 15 minutes. The 30-45 min window stays at a 13% goal probability.
demo_data.scenario_phase3: The second half opens up, in line with the data: the 45-60 min (19%), 60-75 min (20%) and 75-90 min (22%) windows account for most of the goals, with Monaco scoring 30% of their goals in the 45-60 min window. The simulated final score, with 2-1 as the central scoreline, takes shape in the last third of the match, PSG scoring 30% of their goals in the 75-90 min window.

demo_data.fatigue_away: Last match 3 days ago - 2 match(es) in 14 days
demo_data.slot_0: Cautious start: PSG score 14% of their goals in this window and Monaco only 11%. The goal probability for this window is 14%, confirming a tight opening in which both teams look to settle tactically.
demo_data.slot_1: Quietest spell of the match: PSG score only 7% of their goals in this window, and Monaco concede just 4% of theirs here. The goal probability drops to 13%, the lowest of any window in the match.
demo_data.slot_2: The pressure builds slightly but stays contained: PSG score 14% of their goals in the 30-45 min window, Monaco 11%. The goal probability is the same as in the previous window (13%), which statistically supports the scenario of under 1.5 goals at half-time.
demo_data.slot_3: The restart after half-time frees up both teams: Monaco score 30% of their goals in this window, PSG 16%. The goal probability jumps to 19%, marking the attacking turning point of the match and explaining why goals are concentrated in the second half.
demo_data.slot_4: Peak intensity in the heart of the second half: PSG score 19% of their goals here, Monaco 24%, and the goal probability reaches 20%. This is the window in which Monaco, ranked #1 away, are most dangerous going forward in this match.
demo_data.slot_5: Explosive finish: PSG score 30% of their goals in this window, their highest share, and the goal probability peaks at 22%. Monaco concede 26% of their goals here, consistent with a central scoreline of 2-1 taking shape in the closing minutes.
demo_data.scorer_138835: Balogun averages 1.18 shots on target/90 and a smoothed conversion rate of 47%, +12 points above the comparison group average (35%), over 8 tracked matches this season with 5 goals. His threat score of 48/100, with a neutral opponent multiplier (1.0), confirms that he is the best-calibrated attacking threat in this match, regardless of the opposition's defensive context.
demo_data.scorer_483: Kvaratskhelia produces 1.74 shots on target/90 and 3.05 shots/90, the highest volume of attempts among the selected likely scorers, with a smoothed conversion rate of 44% against a group average of 35% over 8 matches. His 4 goals in 8 tracked matches and his threat score of 36/100 make him PSG's main source of attacking danger against Monaco (#1).
